ITEM.PTXT: A 2-piece construction with a separate cam journal section has been adopted, simplifying the cylinder head construction.
The lash adjusters are located at the top of the cylinder head, and the lash adjuster oil supply passage is formed integrally.
A 2-layer metal type cylinder head gasket has been adopted, and shims are provided around the bores to ensure sealing performance and durability.
An acrylic rubber type cylinder head cover gasket with excellent heat and oil resistance has been adopted.

A resin engine cover with sound-absorbing material has been adopted, reducing weight and noise. In addition, a rubber floating method has been adopted for mounting to the engine, eliminating bolts so that the cover can be removed and installed without tools, improving serviceability.

A lightweight aluminum alloy cylinder head cover has been adopted. In addition, sealing performance with the camshaft housing is ensured by fixed-dimension tightening at the outer flange. OCVs (oil control valves) for Dual VVT-i are mounted on the left and right cylinder head covers.
Large baffle plates are built into the left and right head covers. By reducing the flow velocity of the blow-by gas, oil droplets and oil mist are removed, reducing oil carry-over.
An oil delivery pipe is provided to supply lubricating oil, ensuring lubrication of the sliding parts of the roller rocker arms and improving reliability.

A lightweight, highly rigid aluminum alloy cylinder head has been adopted. In addition, the VVT-i oil supply passage has been separated from the cylinder head, simplifying the oil passages in the cylinder head.
A 2-piece construction with a separate cam journal section has been adopted, simplifying the construction of the cylinder head body, reducing weight and improving serviceability.

A pentroof type combustion chamber has been adopted, with the spark plug located almost at the center of the combustion chamber to improve combustion efficiency and knock resistance. In addition, the valve included angle has been narrowed to 25.6°, making the combustion chamber compact.
An efficient cross-flow layout, with the intake on the inside of the V-bank and the exhaust on the outside, has been adopted, and the intake and exhaust ports have a siamese construction.

The intake port shape has been optimized to reduce pressure loss and increase the intake air volume. In addition, the cross-sectional area of the intake port gradually decreases toward the combustion chamber to increase the flow velocity. The shape of the intake port branch is designed to reduce adhesion of injected fuel to the port walls, also reducing emissions.

By adopting long-reach type spark plugs and providing a water jacket between the exhaust port and the spark plug thread, the cooling performance around the spark plugs has been improved, improving knock resistance and combustion.
Plastic region tightening has been adopted for the cylinder head bolts to stabilize the axial force.

An aluminum alloy cylinder block has been adopted to achieve a significant weight reduction, and with a V6 bank angle of 60°, bank offset of 36.6mm and bore pitch of 105.5mm, the overall length and width have been made compact.

The oil pan has a 2-piece construction, with an aluminum alloy oil pan No.1 and a pressed steel oil pan No.2. Oil pan No.1 is an integrated stiffener type that is tightened together with the cylinder block and transaxle case, increasing the rigidity of the entire power plant, reducing vibration and weight.
Appropriate ribs are placed on the outer walls of the cylinder block to increase rigidity.

Centrifugally cast iron liners cast into the block have been adopted for the cylinder liners. A spiny treatment is applied to the outer surface of the cylinder liners (cast iron) to improve adhesion with the cylinder bores (aluminum) and heat dissipation, reducing piston temperature and suppressing bore deformation.
Rigidity has been increased by curving the outer walls of the block and providing reinforcing ribs on the transmission mounting side.
The arrangement of the oil return holes from the cylinder head and the blow-by gas passages has been optimized to smooth oil return and increase the rigidity of the sides of the cylinder block.

Coolant passages formed by drilled passages are provided between the bores, actively cooling the upper part of the cylinder bores, which is easily affected by heat, and making the circumferential temperature distribution of the bore walls uniform. This improves knock resistance and minimizes thermal deformation between the cylinder bores, reducing friction and achieving high performance and low fuel consumption.
Knock sensors are located at 1 locations each on the left and right inside the V-bank, enabling optimum knock control.

Cast iron crankshaft bearing caps have been adopted. They are tightened using plastic region tightening and secured from below with 4 bolts. In addition, they are also tightened together with the cylinder block from both sides to increase rigidity and reduce vibration and noise.

A chain drive system has been adopted, making it maintenance-free. By adopting 9.525mm-pitch high-strength single-row roller chains for the primary and secondary timing chains, the sprockets have been downsized and the engine has been made more compact.

A 2-stage chain system has been adopted, consisting of a primary chain that drives the left and right intake camshafts from the crankshaft and secondary chains that drive the exhaust camshafts from the intake camshafts.

A check ball type chain tensioner with a ratchet mechanism, using both engine oil pressure and spring force, has been adopted for the primary chain tensioner, and compact tensioners that push the chain directly with engine oil pressure and spring force have been adopted for the secondary chain tensioners, constantly applying optimum tension to the timing chains to ensure quietness and reliability.

A lightweight aluminum alloy timing chain cover with high sound insulation has been adopted. The front parts of the cylinder block, camshaft housings and cylinder heads are sealed as a unit. A tooth-skip prevention guide is provided at the crankshaft sprocket to prevent incorrect assembly due to the chain coming off during maintenance. In addition, a service hole for the primary chain tensioner is provided in the timing chain cover for easier maintenance.
Resin material with excellent wear resistance has been adopted for the chain dampers and tensioner slippers.
Dual VVT-i (Dual Variable Valve Timing-intelligent), which controls the intake and exhaust camshafts to the optimum valve timing according to the driving conditions, has been adopted.
The camshafts are made of alloy cast iron. The cam lobes are induction hardened and the surface finish accuracy has been improved, increasing wear resistance and reducing friction.
Nickel alloy with excellent heat resistance has been adopted for the exhaust valve heads to improve durability.

Roller rocker arms have been adopted as the valve train drive mechanism, significantly reducing friction between the cams and sliding parts to lower fuel consumption, and hydraulic lash adjusters have been adopted, eliminating the need for valve clearance adjustment for improved serviceability.
With the adoption of roller rocker arms, the cam profile has a concave radius shape. This increases the valve lift near the start of opening and end of closing, further improving output.
A timing rotor consisting of 3 protrusions for the exhaust side cam position sensor is provided on the exhaust camshaft of each bank.
A cam angle sensor plate for the intake side cam position sensor is provided on the intake side VVT-i controller.

INDICATE.TITLE: Valve Spring Specifications (Common to Intake and Exhaust)

ITEM.PTXT: The rocker arms are cold-forged arms with integrated needle bearings, reducing size and weight, and the rollers are supported by needle roller bearings, significantly reducing friction at the sliding parts and lowering fuel consumption.

An oil delivery pipe method has been adopted to supply lubricating oil to the roller rocker arms. This method reliably supplies lubricating oil to the lubricated parts from above the camshaft, ensuring reliability.
Compact hydraulic lash adjusters have been adopted, constantly eliminating the gap (clearance) between the cams and rocker arms to improve engine quietness.

The lash adjuster is located at the fulcrum on the opposite side of the rocker arm from the valve and uses oil supplied from the cylinder head as hydraulic fluid. The clearance is adjusted by the plunger in the body sliding up and down due to the reaction force of the plunger spring and hydraulic pressure.

When the camshaft rotates clockwise and the cam pushes the rocker arm (during operation), a load is applied to both the valve and the plunger. At this time, the plunger tends to be pushed in, but the check ball closes, so the plunger stops. Therefore, the rocker arm tilts clockwise with the top of the plunger as a fulcrum, pushing the valve down.

When the cam passes its peak, the rocker arm begins to rise due to the force of the valve spring, but because the spring force of the valve spring also acts on the lash adjuster, the hydraulic pressure in the high-pressure chamber is maintained.

When the valve closes (end of operation), the oil in the high-pressure chamber is released from its pressurized state. At this time, valve clearance tends to occur, but the spring force of the plunger spring causes the plunger to push up the rocker arm, keeping the valve clearance at zero at all times. At the same time, the volume of the high-pressure chamber increases, creating a pressure difference with the low-pressure chamber; when it exceeds the spring force of the check ball spring, the check ball lowers to open the oil passage, and oil flows from the low-pressure chamber into the high-pressure chamber in preparation for the next operation (standby state).
A highly efficient vane type VVT-i controller with low friction during operation has been adopted.

The intake side is a 3-vane type and the exhaust side is a 4-vane type. When the engine is stopped, the intake side vanes are locked by a lock pin in the most retarded position, and the exhaust side vanes in the most advanced position.
An advance assist spring is provided in the exhaust side VVT-i to assist torque in the advance direction so that the lock pin engages securely when the engine is stopped.

Based on the signals from each sensor, the engine control computer controls the hydraulic pressure applied to the advance and retard chambers inside the VVT-i controller through the OCVs (oil control valves) mounted on the cylinder head covers, continuously varying the phase of the intake and exhaust camshafts.
Advancing and retarding the intake and exhaust valves provides the following effects.

The position of the spool valve is controlled by the duty signal from the engine control computer so that the valve timing is always optimum. When the engine is stopped, the spool valve is held by spring force in the most retarded position on the intake side and in the most advanced position on the exhaust side, in preparation for the next start.

When the spool valve of the OCV moves to the position shown in the illustration according to the signal from the engine control computer, hydraulic pressure is applied to the advance side and the camshaft rotates toward the advance side.

When the spool valve of the OCV moves to the position shown in the illustration according to the signal from the engine control computer, hydraulic pressure is applied to the retard side hydraulic chamber and the camshaft rotates toward the retard side.

The engine control computer calculates the target advance angle according to the driving conditions and performs control. After the target timing is set, the timing is held by keeping the OCV in the neutral position unless the driving conditions change. This adjusts the valve timing to any target position while preventing unnecessary outflow of engine oil.
Lightweight, high-rigidity aluminum alloy pistons have been adopted.

Sintered forged connecting rods with high strength and little weight variation have been adopted to ensure high reliability. The connecting rod caps are tightened by nutless plastic region tightening, reducing the size of the big end.

A forged 4-journal, 5-balance weight type crankshaft has been adopted, reducing weight while reducing vibration and noise through optimum placement of the balance weights. In addition, the fillets are induction hardened to ensure sufficient strength.

Friction has been reduced by narrowing the connecting rod bearings and crankshaft bearings. In addition, aluminum alloy has been adopted for the bearing lining material, and the lining surface is resin coated, achieving both wear resistance and seizure resistance.

ENTRY.PTXT: Center Distance Between Big and Small Ends [mm]

ITEM.PTXT: The pistons have been made lighter by optimizing the cast-out area above the outside of the pin bosses and the skirt shape. In addition, the area of the piston skirt has been reduced (asymmetrical left and right), and a striated finish and resin coating with excellent seizure resistance have been applied, reducing noise and friction.

A tapered squish combustion chamber is provided on the piston top to achieve stable combustion, and together with the pentroof type combustion chamber on the cylinder head side, a high compression ratio has been achieved, providing both high performance and low fuel consumption. In addition, oil jet cooling has been adopted to reduce piston temperature.
Friction has been reduced by making each piston ring thinner and lowering its tension.
Wear resistance has been ensured by applying an alumite treatment to the top ring groove.

Alumite treatment: A process that electrochemically thickens the oxide film formed when aluminum oxidizes. This oxide film is chemically stable and relatively hard, so it is applied to improve wear resistance.
A serpentine belt drive system, in which all accessories are driven by 1 belt, has been adopted, shortening the overall engine length, reducing weight and improving serviceability.

An automatic tensioner for the V-ribbed belt has been adopted, extending the life of the belt and accessories, making them maintenance-free and improving serviceability when removing and installing the belt. The tension of the V-ribbed belt is kept at the appropriate value by the coil spring built into the automatic tensioner.
A torsional damper pulley has been adopted for the crankshaft pulley to reduce torsional vibration of the crankshaft.

A PCV hose and PCV valve are provided to forcibly introduce blow-by gas into the intake system and burn it, preventing blow-by gas containing large amounts of HC from being released into the atmosphere. A fresh air circulation type has been adopted, in which fresh air is introduced from the air cleaner hose through the right bank head cover and blow-by gas is discharged to the surge tank through the left bank head cover.

Under light load, blow-by gas is drawn into the intake manifold through the PCV valve by intake manifold vacuum and burned. In addition, the internal pressure of the crankcase is regulated, and fresh air is introduced from the cylinder head cover.
Under heavy load, to prevent blow-by gas containing large amounts of HC from being released into the atmosphere, it is forcibly introduced into the intake system by intake manifold vacuum and burned.
Dedicated oil return passages and blow-by gas passages are provided in the cylinder block and cylinder heads, improving oil return and reducing oil carry-over.
The engine is supported by 4 mounts (front, right, left and rear), and the placement and characteristics of each engine mount have been optimized to reduce noise and vibration.
